definition: The total of the data values divided by how many there are, written $\bar{x}$.
The middle value of the data in order; for an even number of values, the mean of the middle two.
The value that occurs most often in a data set.
The value halfway along a class, $\frac{a + b}{2}$ for the class $a \le x < b$, used to stand for every value in that class.
For grouped data with equal class widths, the class with the highest frequency.
How spread out a data set is, measured by the range, the interquartile range or the standard deviation.
One of the values that cut ordered data into quarters: a quarter of the data lies below the lower quartile $Q_{1}$, and three quarters below the upper quartile $Q_{3}$.
A measure of the typical distance of the data values from their mean, written $\sigma$; it is the square root of the variance.
The mean of the squared distances of the data values from their mean, written $\sigma^{2}$: the square of the standard deviation.
